Maaika: Maaika is never friends with her ex-partners. Indeed, several of them have taken out restraining orders against her.
Mabel: "Oh, okay then," she says, dolefully. "I'll go." And off she goes at a gentle pace carrying her two wooden pales, as she begins her 5 mile round-trip to the well.
Macaela: If ever a politician wanted to dig up the dirt on an opponent then he or she could do worse than looking to one of his or her most underrated advisors, Macaela. Sure, on the surface she's cute and attentive and diligent, and she looks fab at all the cocktail parties, but behind this façade is a rather savvy and subversive operator. As a teenager her parents had no idea what she really got up to.
Macarena: Macarena's entire physiology produces so much energy that her hair has no choice but to be curly. Here is another bouncy, sexy soul who, when you say her name, spins around, eyes wide open and expectant. This is her entire approach to life. Amen.
Macey: If ever confronted with a male buffoon at some pub, bar or restaurant, who is attempting to swoon her with a pick-up line like, "Wow, you've got  a good body!", in very short order the afforementioned buffoon will find himself lying on the floor, clutching at his crotch and writhing in agony. And fair enough, too.
Machelle: Machelle is a funny chick. She also knows how to pull-in all her resources to get the job done. Yes yes, her name is spelt weirdly but so what? It has forged an independent temperament and a well-rounded sense of fun and playfulness. Yes, she can argue the house down and don't for one second think it'll bother her if you tell her you're in a bad mood, expecting her to do something about it. She's just as likely to tell you to fuck off and come back when you're not. Her happiness is her responsibility and she expects the same of others. Amen to that.
Mackenzie: Oh, goodness me. We can't say that she's always slightly hysterical for that is overstating it, but she certainly doesn't mind a healthy slice of in-your-face human interaction. The other thing she loves is designer labels. (This is one of her only flaws.)
Macushla: "Ma-who?" most people say after meeting her. But, unlike many in the Kingdom she is unbothered by their reaction. Indeed, Macushla is unbothered by most things unless they are actually important to the health or well-being of her or her loved ones/colleagues. She's an extremely fair-minded lass who is loved by just about everyone, although for some reason that thought only occurs to them after she's out of the room. Weird, huh?
Madale:
Impossible to be depressed around, Madale turns up as another guest of the wedding, looking like a million dollars and with a smile to match. By looking at her, one might imagine she'd have a good time, drink a few champagnes, maybe even get out on the dance floor for a song or two, and then toddle off home in a taxi before it gets too late.  

Here's a tip: If the wedding reception is slightly dull, you might only spot Madale by following the music way down at the back of the garden, all hidden away. Not only has she stolen away three members of the band and a case of bubbly, she's secretly usurped most of the fun people from guest list, including the bride. And no one even saw her do it!
Maddie:
Cheeky but not rude. 

Funny but not a comedienne.

Always happy.

Always lovely.

Maddie is way more capable than she imagines.
Maddy: Maybe she's a Madison, perhaps she's a Madeleine, or even more infrequently, she might even just be Maddy. Anyway, it matters not. If the world knows of this lass by only this name, you can expect that in front of you is a sexy little optimist who has been afforded an enviable path through life. She smiles easily, she's no idiot and when she gets around to it, because let's face it, she's busy, Maddy is a passionate partner and lover. Not bad eh? (But, as ever, if she's usually called some other name - like those first two - forget the whole paragraph and go check out those names. Phew.)
Madeleine: Yes, I know, you're the same as that other one. But, do you know, you're not really. Anyway, enjoy girls……(Madeline/Madeleine: A true thespian, be it on the street, in the lounge room or on the stage. She refuses to wear her hair short.) And yes, I know, you'll need to see 'Madison' in order to get the ‘Maddy’ tale but sometimes life is like that, so suck it up and enjoy it, is my advice! Management.
Madeline: Yes, I know, you're the same as that other one. But do you know, you're not really. Anyway, enjoy girls……(Madeline/Madeleine: A true thespian, be it on the street, in the lounge room or on the stage. She refuses to wear her hair short.) And yes, I know, you need to visit 'Madison' in order to get the 'Maddy' tale but sometimes life is like that, so suck it up and enjoy it, is my advice! Management.
Madelyn: Doesn't tolerate bad manners, dodgy friends or rude men. For such a formal and well-groomed name, this girl regularly gets her hands dirty and she isn't beyond sticking the boot in, if need be. She's a passionate lover, but take heed you prospectives out there, you wont be able to just waltz on in if she gives you that look. You’ll need to prepare yourself.
Madhavi:
Repeating her name several times is like uttering a 3000-year-old meditation mantra. Madhavi, Madhavi......She has more time than she knows what to do with, she's never early to anything, she has a big, beautiful smile and when she hugs she really hugs. Change: she was built for it and as for a career......what the hell does that mean?

(Her friends secretly believe that when she dreams she levitates herself off the bed.)
Madigan:
Don't you love equestrian events? Man and beast in feats of conjoined power and beauty. Show Jumping - that's what we like up here in the commentary box and here comes our leader now, Madigan, on her trusty steed, Johnny Come Lately. 

Only two jumps left and so far it's been a perfect run. If she can clear these two then victory is surely hers. 

Here she comes now...and OH NOOOOO!!....Johnny Come Lately stuttered just before the jump....oh my goodness!....Horse and rider cleared the hurdle but Madigan has almost fallen! She's grasping onto the horses neck from underneath! How ridiculous! The horse is continuing on!...you can see the exertion on Madigan's face, depserately holding on. Oh no! Johnny Come Lately is preparing for the final jump! He won't make it! Oh heavens above...crash, bang wallop they go into the final jump, head first together. The two of them resemble a rugby scrum. Heaven's to Betsy, Brian! Did you see that?

I did George.

Well, there goes the gold medal. Why go over a fence when you can go through it, hey what! Thankfully Madigan and Johnny Come Lately are okay. She's in the water and he is standing above her, sniffing her hat. What a memeorable performance! (This kind of thing seems to happen to Madigan all the time and thankfully she’ll never give up.)
Madison: A spoilt brat if she remains Madison. Maddy, on the other hand, is absolutely adorable.
Madonna: Messy, and we're not talking about her bedroom.
Mae: Mae has never stolen anything in her life, aside from a pale of milk during the drought in 1982, but people’s lives were in peril.
Maeve: Ever heard of necromancy? We hadn’t either until we got chatting to Maeve. She doesn’t tell too many people about it, as you can imagine, let alone any men (or women) she might be interested in. Maeve is one cool cat, you understand, as well as being a very enlightened soul. She’s rarely rushing and she never forces anything, and these traits alone make her utterly beguiling.
Magdalena: We don't get it - Jesus is dead, right? Although, hang on. Did he exist? He must've. Anyway, Magdalena, just like Rhonda a little later, is a hopeless romantic. M, a tiny chunk of advice and you can ignore it if you like, ensure you are happy within yourself and don't expect some man/woman/whoever to fill up the holes for you!
Magdallen: The name of a rather serious and gorgeous-looking model sitting for a nude drawing class. She has long brunette hair.
Magenta: Not really that athletic, Magenta warms more to psychological pursuits. She has a gazillion spiritual guide books in her house and Tibetan prayer flags draped across her verandah, which overlooks the vegie’ patch. Big smile. Flowing dresses.
Maggie:
Option A:  The beautiful black, sweet-natured Labrador dog that slobbers over everything. She has the softest ears in the world.

Option B:  Maggie is that woman all women secretly aspire to. She hasn’t been brainwashed by the beauty companies, she’s messy, her car is a fucking joke, she laughs loudly (snorting occasionally if it’s really funny), she bears no grudge and she harbours no regrets. She doesn’t believe in God but if, someday, somehow, she was canonised and turned into a saint, her reaction would be to nod quietly and say, “I like the sound of that,” before bursting into more laughter. Maggie.
Mags: Mags is no rock star, she’s not a leader of society, she’s not a criminal and she’s neither abusive nor selfish. What she is, is friendly and funny.
Mahalia: Woah betide anyone who stands between her and that dress she's suddenly spotted in her favourite dress shop. If she gets it, all will be well. If someone beats her to it, however, that lady may well be pursued at pace, with random items thrown at her (in line with the shrieking abuse) in at attempt to inflict physical pain and/or damage. Ain't no riding off quietly into the sunset with this one.
Mahlia:
Option A:  As a city girl, Mahlia gives more of herself than most people in any room she happens to be in. She's not a mover and a shaker, she's more a listener and a soother. 


Option B:  As a country girl, she can shoot, she can change a tyre with one hand, she can help a mare give birth and, to be honest, she hasn't got time to listen to some bleating heart who is whinging about shit that, quite frankly, does not matter.
Maia:
Option A: Yes, it's true, her reputation is justified. When we caught up with Maia, in her temple in Eastern India, we had to wait in a queue 100 metres long. Luckily, we were permitted entry into the one and only yoga-cum-mediation session that she gives each year. I don't know how she does it. Everyone was aching and wincing in pain, but you should have seen her up the front - the smile never left her face and not once did she break out in a sweat. 
(Note: She doesn't handle life in the city very well. All the pollutants and the noise drive her quite batty!)

Option B: The lazy palm tree overhanging a calm, pristine Fijian reef.
Mairead: Look, we're not Catholics up here in Management, indeed, we follow life in whatever denomination you want to ascribe to it, but if ever those Vatican twits decided it was time to open their minds and get REAL by permitting the naming of a female Pope, then Mairead should be the one. Why? Because she dispenses with all ceremonial bullshit, she loves people and encourages everyone to be the best they can be, and the creme della creme is that she seeks to find positives in the tragedies that occasionally befall us all.
Maisie: Oh boy, so now we know. The team up here in the commentary box imagined she was going to be a skilled and courageous player, but no one suspected this…
Maitri: Maitri will sit across from you, encourage you to settle down and clear your mind, before she looks deeply into your eyes. Don't be scared when she does this. She's looking into your soul and that's why she's smiling and I promise you it'll be worth it....
Maja: Expectant and optimistic, Maja is something of a trail-blazer. That's not to say she's in your face when things don't turn out as she expected - she's never that angry, mostly because she rarely experiences anger. Maja is a very intelligent and savvy lass, and so she usually knows people and situations, and how things are going to turn out in advance. Best of all though, she is a happy soul who wants to play. "After all," she'll tell you, "isn't that why we're here?"
Majbritt: Leap without looking - no chance. Majbritt evaluates everything. She ponders a course before she enters in into the navigating computer. She analyses the nutrient value of each ingredient before she cooks. She thinks about the consequences of her words and her actions and if the European Union gets any closer to splitting apart, they could probably use someone like Majbritt to help them try and make sense of the mess.
Makayla: A thinking girl who would've made an excellent fitter and joiner had she not joined the army. She's no where near as 'girly' as you might expect and she can certainly handle herself.
Makenna: What a wonderful tonic she is. Barely a single second does she either waste or lament, and one seems to follow the other. The optimism and power she exudes are infectious and many flock to her as a result. Makenna is a risk-taker as well as being the intelligent clown, and yes, all the boys love Makenna, whether she’s into them or not.
Makenzie: Makenzie, tell me, what exactly is it that you're waiting for?.......
Mako: Japanese. Apart from this making her a lover of fish, it also makes her very gracious.
Mala: Mala's handwriting has a large, rounded style, she can't reverse a car to save her life and she's happiest in and around food. Big smile. Big hips. Frizzy hair.
Malala:
You start with a hum of intent and then you are immediately opened up from start to finish, with nowhere sarcastic or nasty to go. Pure honesty from an intense and pure heart: this is what Malala brings for us. 
She asks of you, “Are you strong enough?”

It’s a good question…
Malia: The name of a clean, green, healthy apple.
Malieha: A pacifist who, one day, will stand on own two feet and roar!
Malini: It's true that we all create our own luck, but Malini is blessed with a staggering amount of it. I wonder if her parents prayed to the Hindu gods? Anyway, Malini is calm and lovely and funny but, yes, if you want a project to work then don't stand here talking to me. Go and talk to Malini.
Maliya: No, she's not cutthroat in her delaings with people/business/life. She can't (nor does she wish to) run that fast. Indeed, does she run at all? Lying on the beach - that's her thing at the moment, which points to the fact that a tan is important. But, girl, don't let it affect your health. Management.
Mallory: Friends with Philippa, Georgia and Anna. Indeed, that about sums this girl up.
Malyce:
Does Malyce strike like a cobra, asking no questions and taking no prisoners? Mmmmm, not really. She strikes more like a friendly cow sticking its head over the fence, having been offered a handful of fresh juicy grass. Indeed, confrontations aren't really her gig, which goes for a lot of people. But, she has a stack of friends and she's more than happy to skip through the tulips without a care in the world.

(Note: she is way smarter than she lets on.)
Mandy: Perhaps she once suffered from full lips and an empty head, but not for long. Mandy may not be the most elegant player in the outfit, but she’s honest, she’s a funny and sensual creature, and it takes her half a second to suss situations out. She’s definitely too honest for politics because toeing the line is basically impossible.
Mandy-Jane: She's a nightmare to play pool with because at the break she quite literally tries to hit the white ball as hard as she possibly can.
Maneesha: Humble and friendly by default, Maneesha has a warm smile.
Mannela: Yep, the table top is smooth and new and it looks great, but have a look underneath. There's chewing gum and different styles of screws, the legs are even made of different wood, yet it's a great table. The moral to the story is that Mannela isn't a normal, boring table at all. She gets up to all sorts of hanky panky but she doesn’t feel the need to tell anyone, that's all. Not even her friends. They wouldn't believe her anyway.
Manon: The name of an apron as worn by a Belgian peasant woman in a village kitchen that is gripped by a freezing northern European winter, 300 years ago.
Manuela: Manuela is overflowing with love, musicality and recipes. Need we say anymore? And she doesn't shave her armpits, which, frankly, the crew in the commentary box quite admire.
Manuella: Manuella, the crew up here do apologise, but you and your twin sister above are the same. Please check out Manuela. (Okay, so you shave your armpits more. Good for you! We love you both, anyway. Management.)
Mara:
Not often does a human exit the womb and be ready to function as a mature adult within 20 minutes. Mara is one of these people. It's as if she was fed special maturity-enzymes in her amniotic fluid. Perhaps her mother played classical music up against her belly, we'll never know, but the result is a woman rarely flustered and usually content. Immune to peer group pressure, Mara will find her quite eccentric little niche in life and you'll barely see her for dust. 

(Note: If she's studying DO NOT DISTURB.)
Marayke: Here is another case of a name being so ‘out there’ that this is exactly where her destiny took her. Marayke is a sensuous mystery. The last time anyone heard from her she was studying gorillas in Uganda. Has anyone heard anything since?
Marcella: Marcella is no farm plough, put it that way. She dabbles in the stock market, at least she does if she's single, she has an extensive collection of classical music and she loves the theatre.
Marcelle: "What was that?" she asks, spinning around like lightning to see if the topic of gossip was her.
Marcia: Marcia whinges heaps, sometimes. In life she is polite and particular, she finishes what she begins 61% of the time and once in a while someone needs to sneak up on her and push her over. The surprise will do her good, but be warned. Afterwards she’ll either see the funny side of it or try to club you in the head. Irrespective, her reaction is worth watching.
Marcy: A gifted mathematician and physicist. There are planets out there beyond Pluto that need discovering, not to mention the sun’s incredible ejections of plasma whose effect on the Earth needs further investigation. Indeed, we’re lucky to have her.
Mardi: Like a well-tuned engine in a very expensive and gorgeous-looking sportscar, Mardi never backfires, she knows exactly what she's capable off, which is generally quite a lot, and all most people want to do when they get near her is rub their face over her baby-smooth duco. How is it some people have this effect on the rest of us? It's a good question. Mardi, the girl, is very centred and compassionate and yes, the world around her tends to fly with her and never against her, which opens up plenty of doors. As we keep saying, she must have done some good deeds in her previous reincarnations because this life is all about THE HOLIDAY!
Maree: Garlic, and if you don’t love the stuff please leave the kitchen immediately. “Chop Chop!” she says, with a smile. “Let’s go!”
Maretta: Pissed off she gave up fags, Maretta stomps around like Fran, except she often has something like a scowl on her face. She just needs something to get her teeth into, that’s all.
Marg: Marg also goes by the names of Mrs. Reliable and Mrs. Thank Christ That’s Over With.
Margaret: An Australian sheep dog. A Border Collie. A legend. Loved by all and feared by sheep. What would we do without her? What would the nation do without her?
Margaret-Anne: Like a very dry and very rare chardonnay, Margaret-Anne is appreciated by only a select few and often she is a drink that takes some airing-out before the full flavour is permitted to come through. And she’s not cheap. Margaret-Anne is occasionally an insatiable beast in bed and she appreciates her children having good table manners.
Margarita: The name of a huge multi-coloured beach-ball that is tossed about by thirty male and female models, who happen to be gleefully running down a sand dune in the name of making a TV ad for Coca-Cola.
Margery: How is it that, in the movies, when in digsuise out there on the street or inside some organised little civilian life the superheroes are never recognised? Even their names are enough to divert suspicion. For instance, look at Margery. Say it again, Margery. Who would have thought, eh?
Margherita: Margherita tends to be all or nothing. She is artistic, she never looks the same two days in a row and if she ever took the time to write a book about the lovers in her life it would make for hilarious reading. Luckily it probably wouldn't be short either. Amen.
Margie: If you’re in a room and she’s in the one, next door, if she laughs you’ll know because you won’t be able to concentrate on what you are doing, or watching. On a quiet night you’ll even hear her if she’s inside at the front of the house and you’re out in the backyard.
Margo: Thank God! A woman who doesn't mind so much that her name is spelt differently… we hope. (Note: Margo, please visit Margot for the full skinny.)
Margot: Margot is as sexy as hell but there are no beg pardons here: Got a problem? Go to Margo. Her honesty may be too much for some but the world needs her.
Margrith: How many splinters has Margrith removed from her grandchildren and children over the years? Hundreds, probably. It got so bad at one point that kids would wail whenever they were near her because they presumed that her presence meant impending pain. (Later in life, of course, they came to understand how well she held the family together.)
Mari: Mari dislikes it when the plan is altered having only just begun.
Maria: Her mum taught her to cook and that’s great, but that isn’t one five hundredth of the story. And she loves with all her might.
Mariam: Mariam is one of those girls who, despite never joining any kind of Frequent Flyer Program, always gets offered a free upgrade to First Class whenever she travels. Maybe it’s her smile, perhaps it’s that serene, gorgeous vibe she puts out, we don’t know. Better than that, Mariam is here to help the rest of us be better people and to get in touch with our deeper selves. Not bad eh?
Marian: How is it some woman manage to radiate light? We don’t know either…
Marianna: “Oh, daaarling. It’s sooooo good to seeeeeee you....!!!! Here.....crack this. Oooohhh, you look simply divine!!” .....etc, etc.
Marie:
"I don't care that the creek is flooded. We're going to go down there and get those horses and you're coming with me, do you hear? You left them there when I told you to bring them in, so you're coming to help. I don't want to hear any arguments. This is important."
Indeed, Marie is strong but she’s fair. God love her.
Marie-Clare: The elegant, refined and gorgeous-smelling city girl who dresses well and speaks very clearly. Ture, she only recently discovered that butter and cream come from cows but fuck it, nothing's perfect. Her man better have excellent table manners though and at least be just a little chivalrous!
Marie-Helene:
No matter your persuasion, by the end of saying her name you already see the truth of her, don’t you.
Her personality swirls around you like a big warm glove, full of heat and compassion. Trivial people and events are never on her radar and she aspires always to invent and to explore. Marie-Helene lives her life like one of those dreams where you’re just about flying, your feet touching the ground only occasionally…
Marie-Rose: Marie-Rose, if your husband forgets either your birthday or your anniversary again you have our permission to divorce him. You're a dramatic, sexual and loud creature and you deserve more attention than this!
Marieka: Educated, travelled and brilliant, Marieka is a picture of pointed grace and eccentric humour until she hits the bedroom, where upon she transforms into a creature so sensually mysterious and wonderful that we can barely discuss her properly here. The End.
Mariel: Mariel plans everything elaborately and properly.
Mariela: The lead actress who is irate if, at the end of the performance, the audience doesn't seek an encore.
Mariella: As a Bird of Paradise in a past life, Mariella loves drama and she does a pretty solid job of concocting it, seemingly from totally placid and serene situations. It's quite a gift, in lots of ways. Yes, once she was threatened with incarceration in a mental institution but her looks, as well as her capacity to think quickly on her feet, got her off.
Marielle: Marielle is a tugboat for all of her friends. Indeed, many of them are only her friend because they need one.
Marija: It's World War 2 and Marija is busy. Apart from everything else, in the past 6 months she's smuggled three RAF POWs into Spain on horseback, she's transported a coding machine across the Rhine in a small boat, which, unbeknown to her or anyone will shorten the war by 8 months, she’s drugged to death at least 9 German spies and right now she's wearing a red velvet dress at a small Berlin club, where she's dancing with a high-ranking Nazi. Little does he know he's not long for this world, but Marija is. She's still got work to do and, by God, she hates nasty ‘Nazis’, of any shape.
Marika: With the subtle eccentricities of a Northern European background, Marika is more committed and conservative than you might expect.
Marilyn: Marilyn is another woman who can’t help escape a certain kind of maleness, but she is a sensual woman and one whose tough and dignified skin hides a girly sense of fun.
Marina: Marina’s line of argument is occasionally out of whack with the truth, which is a shame because she’s a passionate soul on the continual march for righteousness.
Marine: Bob Dylan wrote a lyric about her, lifetimes ago - something to do with being on the brink of destruction. But, Marine, don't listen to all that bullshit. You're sexy, and when you're relaxed you're funny, and you'll figure it out.
Marion: Marion is a deeply sensual and funny woman. At a quick glance you might think that she’d be morose and slightly timid, but that couldn’t be further from the truth. Marion will take your breath away.
Maris: The only time her and her husband argue is when he's driving and she's got the map. The last time she became so irate that she tossed the map from the car before insisting he let her out so she could hitchhike home, which she did. (True to form, the make-up sex four hours later was spectacular!)
Marisa: Marisa gets very confused by electronic gadgets and only recently has had the internet put on at her house. Not that she uses it much.
Marisca: No, Marisca doesn't just turn up folks. She can't help but stand up, stand proud and be noticed in any crowd. She makes a wonderful friend/lover/ally/work colleague, but her sheer lack of anonymity means a life in the secret service is out of the question.
Marise: Marise enjoys her life and almost never attracts carnage and chaos. Sure, she would dispute this, but you need to ignore that. She’s a wonderful mentor, in lieu of her predominantly calm nature, and she is a gentle and giving lover.
Mariska: Mariska lives for Burning Man, Nevada.
Marissa: Highly active and therefore generally lean of limb and lovely, Marissa could be the radio DJ with a high-pitched voice who laughs at nothing and laughs at nothing (which isn’t perfect), as easily as she might be the sharp-talking business owner who can’t handle watching a second wasted. Either way, Marissa relishes being the Queen of the Stage.
Marita: Marita is an energetic woman who harnesses that energy in being able to fix or clean-up almost any situation that requires it, and it assists her in being a wonderful friend who dishes out prudent advice when needed. (She dances on tables when she’s drunk, and we’re not just saying that as some kind of humorous metaphor.)
Marj: A more relaxed and potent version of her daughter, below.
Marjorie: A splendid country mother who wins the Shepherd’s Pie baking competition at the show, each year. It’s just too delicious.
Marl:
Gentlemen, remember that Marl is a woman and sometimes women like to be grabbed in a passionate fashion, then looked in the eye and kissed well. Marl doesn't get anywhere near enough of that. So, what are you waiting for?
The End.
Marlee: Like a scenario out of a movie, if a nuclear warhead detonated above Sydney, for instance, then all that would humanly remain would be a scared and filthy little girl with bright tough eyes, and whose name was Marlee.
Marlene: The beautiful pragmatist with a wonderful sense of humour. Marlene is possibly the unsung backbone of rural life in any English-speaking country.
Marley: Where as someone like Clarissa probably should work for them, Marley does work for Medicine Sans Frontier because she possesses a giant heart and she wants to do more than sit around and watch.
Marli: The solo dancer. And very happy, she is.
Marlie:
Marlie’s presence is  refreshing and surprising like a dunk in a waterfall. No matter how old she is, Marlie will look at you like she’s just arrived on earth, keen to absorb and to hear anything new or interesting. She therefore loves travel more than most, not to mention a nice, summery holiday romance, and she only gets perplexed if you ask her what she does. Because she’s immersed in the moment so deeply, it’s a question that doesn’t always make immediate sense to her. 
“Well, I’m here talking to you,” she’ll say with a cute and confused smile. “Is that what you mean?”
Indeed, it might pay just to watch her and film what she gets up to next because we don’t know either...
Marlies: Highly educated and with a large ego, Marlies contemplates the effect of her words before speaking them.
Marliese: Short, sexy spiky hair. She walks quickly, looking determined, even when buying a humble loaf of bread. (And we’re not talking normal bread here. We’re talking gluten-free, seeds, organic, etc.)
Marlin: No, she may not be from around these parts but Marlin is a woman who knows how to use her powers.
Marlo: A polite and educated female usher at the classical music concert hall. And yes, she only works there so she can get paid to attend.
Marnie:
You look down into the deep dark well and you yell, “Helloooooooooooo……….”
You listen, waiting for the echo to return to you and tell you how deep it is.  How deep is it? How deep is the well?
Marny: Marny is very similar to Marnie, above, apart from one very important fact - Marny's well has a torch at the top as well as a set of metal steps which lead down into the darkness. If you wanted to, therefore, you could quite easily climb down to Marny's depths. Remember though, it’s still an awfully long way down. You got a cut lunch?
Marslie: Rash decisions aren't usually her thing and Marslie therefore enjoys most moments and emotions to the full extent. She's like a bar of expensive dark chocolate, in that regard.
Martelle:
Flights of semi-deluded fancy? 
You bet. 
Notions of working long and hard at some dedicated career?
Forget it.
Expectations of rich suitors tending to her every whim?
Every bloody day.
A story of unfulfilled potential?
Yes! 
Unless….hang on….did she go to acting school ? She did?….well, forget all that. Aside from her run-ins with the paparazzi she’ll be fine.
Martha:
Standard, normal, average: these are some of the phrases one might conjure up when you say the name Martha. 
What baloney!
Martha is her own woman, true enough, and yes, in all likelihood she was born in a country farmhouse, but that was then and this is now. Martha stands up for what she believes in, she laughs hard, at times doubling over with sore stomach muscles, and she couldn’t give a shit where she is at the time. Her friends adore her to the point of not knowing what they’d do without her and when (not if) she meets that person who, for her, radiates that loving light, she will protect and love that person with all her might. Onya Martha.
Martina: "Why would I care what people say about me?" she says, more than asks. "Actually, why does anyone?" Martina is busy being Martina, and that, ladies and gentlemen, is a many splendid thing.
Martine: Is she a mild misfit or just a magnet for eerie coincidences? She might even be positively schizophrenic but beneath the confusion there lies a kind heart and a deeply sexual undertone.
Mary: The thick woollen jumper that you put on when it’s freezing cold. She’s comforting and intelligent, sensual and unusual, she smells incredible, she’s everyone’s favourite and she’s the dark horse of the century – no question. However, Mary does carry a hidden burden....
Mary-Beth:
The kind of girl who, no matter how often she fucks up in the office, is just too funny, too cute and too nice to fire. Life is boring without her, so screw the bottom line. 
The End.
Mary-Jane: The Trombone that was bought at a second hand shop for $50.
Mary-Jean: In a past life Mary-Jean was a fighter pilot in the Russian airforce during World War 2. Girls were permitted to become such things, thankfully, and Mary-Jean was no slouch. We know that because she was never shot down. Here in the new millennium, therefore, you can expect MJ to be incredibly capable. She possesses spunk, is a brilliant lateral thinker and she makes loves in public parks if she feels like it. What more can one say?
Mary-Jo: Busy and reasonably formal, Mary-Jo is highly capable and extremely bright. She gathers no dust, she speaks her mind and all office/corporate settings function better when she’s around. Mary-Jo is a lot less serious than she looks and only her lovers know how passionate and delicious she can be.
Mary-Lee: Once a year Mary-Lee flies to New York for two weeks where she hangs out at the best jazz clubs in town, smoking big fat cigars with all the big fat black men.
Mary-Lou: Do we expect a mystery or not? Is she wise? Is she a dim-witted buffoon? No one is sure, but she is definitely outrageously happy most of the time, clothed or otherwise. Her perfect job is therefore working in a lolly shop.
Mary-Louise: They don't call her the Dam Buster for nothing. She can party (or at least, she did once upon a time), she takes charge, she never loses an argument (which is mighty irritating during those rare occasions when even she knows she's  wrong) and she doesn't care how many cars are hooting their horns at her during some parking fiasco or other. Mary-Louise was plonked here on Earth to act as a shining example of what you can do if you believe in yourself. If I had pause to think, she might also kiss you in to next week, but that's another story and one reserved for only a very brave few. Amen.
Mary-Lynn: Like many creatures in the Kingdom, Mary-Lynn has hidden spurs which are used to protect her from predators and extreme competitors. On top of that she sees outcomes long before anyone else and therefore makes early preparations accordingly, hence all the fussing about. Indeed, it’s why her spurs aren’t employed all that frequently.
Mary-Rose: Mary-Rose occasionally laments being brought up in a male-dominated world because she is fully aware at how much better the place would be if women like her were in charge. And she's right.
Mary-Royce: No, she doesn't own a roller, but she is a bustling ball of constant, reliable energy. She also regularly attracts unusual, coincidental moments which provide hilarity and calm (in the aftermath). Mary-Royce is also the sort of person who, while rarely a punter of any description, will arrive at the pub late amid a bustling flail of arms and legs, and before she's even sat down has won both the meat tray and the grog raffle. Indeed, this is how her entire life has unfolded.
Maryanne: Soft at the beginning and hard at the finish, Maryanne is the sort of girl that will start a fight just so she can join in. She swears like a cow cocky.
Maryella: Maryella has abundant love in her heart and silly spectacles on her face.
Marzley: Across between a Mars Bar and a ticket to the New Year's party of the year, Marzley is the kind of girl who gets men frothing at the mouth. She's quite clumsy in the kitchen.
Mataj: It's all about preparation for a moment, with this girl. It might be the penalty kick to win a World Cup, the final touches on a dessert produced by one of the great chefs at one of the world's best restaurants, or even a pivotal piece of advice given to a child in a moment of crisis, for Mataj is well considered and exact, right at the death, and right when only the best will do. The trade-off is that outside these critical seconds she's completely relaxed and/or lazy, which is fair enough when you think about it.
Mathilde: With loads of common sense - I know, who would have thought? - Mathilde works well and efficiently, and she therefore gets paid a sum that is comensurate with her efforts.
Matilda: Matilda is too bloody nice and wonderful for her own good.
Matisse: Irrespective of their upbringing, some people, through either luck or design, end up caring for other people more than themselves. You'd imagine that with what Matisse gets offered, and the doors that are available to her, she have danced and laughed her way through Spanish language school in Barcelona over the summer. But no way. She was in the South Sudan organising schedules for Medicine Sans Frontier. No matter that she's covered in dust and no one has showered much lately here, she never loses her sense of humour and never loses that grin.
Mattie: Not many girls could be plucked from society as a winner of the world's weirdest raffle, and pull-off being appointed the Queen of the Land. Mattie could, easily. She's fair-minded, her ego doesn't drive her world, she's compassionate, she looks great in a gown, if not a little embarrassed, she abhors all violence and she assists others to be better people. What more can you ask from a leader?
Maude: Yes, French blood is in there somewhere and the result is startling. Maude, far from being boring, is an extremely passionate and determined girl. If you're lying to her she'll know and don't you dare do that. I wouldn’t talk too much merde either. Yet, behind this curtain is a loving smile that's ready and willing for fun, silliness and saucy times. Bravo Maude.
Maureen: Maureen is skilled at skinning rabbits, she’s a bit naughty after a few glasses of sherry and, whether it’s in the garden tending a new season or at the front door, fending off a tipsy, idiotic and deluded ex-boyfriend, she’s pretty handy with a pitchfork. In short, Maureen tends not to fuck around with matters and she has a wonderful, relaxed sense of humour.
Maurine: As a world famous olive oil infused with rosemary and just a hint of anchovy and lemongrass, Maurine is unique in the culinary world because chefs seem unable to resist ripping their clothes off, covering themselves in the oil and making love in la cucina as soon as the meal is presented. Weird eh? Beautiful and complex, she is, but she's definitely worth getting fired over. And is there a formula for figuring her out?.....(thankfully) NO!
Mauve: Mauve doesn't hobnob with the jewellery-clad twats who get down to the wine bar every Friday night scoping out young men. Mauve likes being with her friends solely for their company, their conversation and their raucous laughter.
Mavis:
DITCH THY WATER BUCKET FAIR MAIDEN, FOR THE DULL DAYS ARE OVER! 
"MAVIS! OH MAVIS!" the crowd cheers. Mavis, my dear, you've toiled for too long tending your family. Sometimes it is possible to do too much. Now, we think it's time that we looked after you. Amen.
Max:
Max is a reasonably normal superstar whose only possible gripe is the maleness that the world attributes to her. Not that she has a gripe, to be honest, because she carries one of the most independent and powerful names in the Kingdom, providing her with intelligence and spunk. 
(Gentlemen, if you believe in marriage you could do a lot worse.)
Maxene: Air Traffic Controller. The fact that she tells jokes with the frequency she does used to spook many of her colleagues in the tower, but she hasn't crashed anyone yet. As a matter of fact, when the chips are down and an aircraft (relative, spouse, friend, neighbour, stranger, animal, anything, anyone) is in distress and in need of assistance, Maxene will put away the jokes and sort out an immediate plan to get that plane on the ground in one piece. Little do the passengers on board ever realise the logistical mountains she's prepared to move in 30 seconds or less.
Maxine: A-type personality, or maybe an A-B. Maxine is highly intelligent, a natural leader and she is enthused by unusual people and preposterous situations.
Maxy: The cheeky, horny, drunk or aggressive version of Max, above.
Maxyne:
Picture this scene inside an operating theatre: A team of 12 medicos are gathered next to a variety of high-tech machines with lots of lights and buttons, the anaesthetist is bent over the head of the unconscious patient and looking content with how things are progressing, and all the nurses are looking slightly concerned behind their  face masks.

Not the surgeon, however. She's sitting off to the side, at the controls of a machine that is performing keyhole surgery, so she's peering into a large TV screen through her spectacles sitting half way down her nose. Fuck knows what she's doing, but she's currently humming in time to the music of ACDC, and no one could imagine she's performing an operation that's only ever been tried once before. And that first one wasn't successful.
After 3 hours of general whispering to herself (and singing), she lets out a big sigh and says, "Right, that oughta' do it. Let's sew him up see how he goes."

Maxyne.
May: May would have had a lot more fun if she’d been in her 20’s during the 60’s, rather than in her 30’s during the 40’s, as was the case, but I suppose there was no food back then. In any case, May is honest, respectable and direct.
Maya: Maya was re-incarnated from a Central American Goddess who lived 1500 years ago in what is known today as Costa Rica. She has perfect olive skin, luscious black hair, a devilish smile in her dark eyes and she holds a PhD in quantum chemistry, which has everything to do with how she was re-incarnated in the first place.
Maye: Maye lies in bed at night, dreaming of the perfect hand of bridge, or maybe the ideal opening set of letters in her next game of Scrabble. Rock climbing, parachuting and deer hunting are none of her business as they predominantly take place outdoors.
Mayelle: Perhaps they need to invent an ambulance-type service where, if a person was feeling a little glum and cold, and needed a good hug and a bowl of hot soup, they could call for assistance. Such a service, if it existed, would be called the Mayelle Modicum. She's a listener and offers sounds advice, and she enjoys people - the more different from her the better - but, it's not a free service and so there are no giveaways here. She has to live too, you know.
Mayim: It's not that she hasn't got friends, she has tons, it's just that people as intelligent AND hilarious as Mayim don't grow on trees. But they're out there. Not that it really matters. Mayim has a busy brain and therefore she is busy in life. She likes everyone unless proven otherwise and the people who don't like her have clearly never met her, and we certainly harbour no desire to meet them.
Mayiwase: (Pron. Maa-why-say) Like many many people, she ain’t originally from around these parts, which is a grand thing (apart from all Kiwis). Anyway, Mayiwase laughs loudly, studies hard and provides a different tweak on how to do things.
MayLing:
Well where do you start? How is it some people can smile at you and immediately put you at peace. I'd suggest it's a gift, who knows, but she'd certainly be fun to live with. 
"What'd you do today?" someone would ask you.
"Oh well," you'd reply, "not much. I went to May Ling's house and watched her make a cup of tea and bake some biscuits."
".....Really? You did that all day?"
"Yep. And I've never been happier."
(It'd go something like that.)
In life therefore May Ling is surrounded by calm, happy people and usually all you want to do is hug her.
Mayomi: With skin the colour of a stunning dancing mare, Mayomi is anything but predictable. She is the kind of girl who enters the room from afar, and though you can't see the door from where you stand, the growing cheers and commotion from that part of the room leave no doubt as to who has arrived. Then, all of a sudden, she'll appear right next to you with a cheeky grin, as happy to see you as you are to see her. Some people do that.
Maytal: Maytal rhymes with Just Right. She has a diamond stud through her nose, potent Israeli blood in her veins and delicious green bliss in her eyes.
McKeeley:
About as subtle as an 18-wheeler gently smashing into the back half of the house while everyone's asleep. Is McKeeley happy? You bet. Will she get up in your face if you spell her name wrong? That too. Does she laugh like a demented, magnificent witch? Damn right she does. Does she give you too much information regularly? Ah huh. And do we love her? 

.....What do YOU reckon.
McKenna: Corporate finance pow-wows and highly charged legal meetings are places you will rarely, if ever, see McKenna. School was never her thing, you see. Like a happy seal, McKenna's real gift is sliding from her towel into the swimming pool at the shiny white resort without spilling her drink. (Come on girl! Stop sliding around in your bikini and get out into the world! It's waiting for you and so are we! - Management)
Meagan: How many ways can you spell a name? Anyway, Meagan is a walking, talking realist, give or take. Slotted in the middle ground between Shazza and Lisa, Meagan goes about her business with a smile. She expects people to be decent, she is popular and she's never been in a fist fight, we think...
Meaghan: Completely underrated, Meaghan has a warm heart and she is true to the bone. Yes, some specimens are perhaps a little more rural in their outlook and expectations, but not all of them. No sir.
Meave: The sparkling, wonderful and understated Ghost Writer.
Mecushla: Mecushla loves driving in Paris because it's the only place on Earth where she can parallel park with ease. Why? Because she can crash into the car in front and the car behind again and again, forward and back, forward and back, bang bang bang bang, until she's in properly. No, there ain't nothing subtle about the hilarious Mecushla.
Meegan: Meegan is great, but you need to explain things to her several times before she understands them. I'm not sure why because she's not an idiot.
Meg: Like any new wooden clothes peg, Meg is elemental, unpolished and she has chores to attend to.
Megan: (Pron. Meg-ann) Megan carries a blunt tomahawk and enjoys chopping wood for long periods. (i.e: she’s fucking persistent.)
Meghan: A fun, laid back girl. Cocky too, in her own weird way. In high school, for instance, no matter if she was inside or outside, when she finished eating an apple she would pin-point the nearest bin, ensure she was at least 15 feet from it and try to lob the core into it. She rarely missed, of course, which really used to piss-off the teachers. By the time the apple core had finished its journey, they would have already filled their lungs with air in preparation for a ritualistic dressing down, which they rarely got to do. She wouldn’t have listened anyway.
Mel: She’s more of a man than Troy, Spencer and Perry put together, but somehow she manages to retain her woman’s sexiness. She’ll often vent any personal frustration by insisting that any friends that happen to be present wrestle her in a no-holds-barred affair. Win or lose, you will be covered in bruises at the finish and you’ll be lucky if you can use your wrist the next day, but she’ll be the first person to buy you a beer at the pub afterwards.
Melanie: Rarely a show off, Melanie’s maze of a name means she’s simply got too much going on to be able to let her ego completely take over the joint, and that’s a good thing. Deep down, Melanie aspires to keep things simple and to make her life as streamlined and manageable as possible. Why this rarely happens we’re not sure. Out on the ground she tries hard and she’s a tremendous team player, and her deep gasps of exhaustion late in the final quarter aren’t a put-on, that’s for sure.
Melany: Melany is lousy on her own and for this reason she craves the company of her friends.
Meliah: Meliah is slightly more aloof than a very cute, female Bugs Bunny. She kind of hangs around and looks all casual, leaning up against the wall with her elbow cocked against her head. She looks like she's never rushed a thing in her life. But, deep down, you know she's as cunning as a funny fox. She's all for giving and having a laugh with people, and she's a flirt, don't you worry about that, and some gag or ridiculous prank is only just around the corner...You can feel it!
Melina: Melina is lovely, although she never accepts your answer as the answer.
Melinda: No, Melinda isn't tomato sauce – although most boys do love her.  Indeed, if anything she's like an intense hit of wasabi. Melinda has an ego which enables her to take the lead in a situation if one is required because she doesn’t mind treading on toes, and her moments of forgetfulness arise only because she occasionally forgets to stand back and look at a position objectively.
Melisa: Melisa isn’t unlike her older and more responsible sister, below, except that she’s more unpredictable. For example, she loves taking pictures of her naked tattooed boyfriend while he’s asleep, which is something Melissa would only do if she was hyper-excited and/or tipsy.
Melissa: Melissa is normal gal with a warm, loving nature and she hardly ever suffers from psychotic episodes.
Melita: Melita reads the rules before she acts and the recipe before she cooks. With a little luck, she will come back in another life as Nancy, and learn how not to do things.
Meliza: We've never seen Meliza on the rostrum. Why is that madame? You've got two arms and two legs like everyone else and we all start the race at the same time. Perhaps a little self-discipline the night before the race, eh?
Mellesa: With only seconds to spare, Mellesa can throw enough gloss where it’s needed such that no one suspects she was either late or flustered. Underpinning her entire character is the knowledge she will always get the shit done that she needs to, and so she isn’t that flustered anyway. Her kids are direct and friendly, and like their mum, they’ll call-out a creep or a weirdo without any prompting whatsoever. It’s quite a skill. Mellesa is definitely a doer.
Mellisa: Yes, Mellisa is capable and dynamic, but the magnitude of her achievements is usually under-appreciated by those around her. The main reason is that Mellisa understands that life is but a series of steps, and where even before a project, task or moment is over, the next one has already begun. So, here she is; Creating good deeds and being there without the fanfare. God bless you Mellisa.
Melody: A rather sexy Juggernaut. Melody is neither a pushover nor is she remotely dull.
Mem: Her name resembles an individual hiccup, so something in her life is going to be seriously out of whack, sometime, but Mem’s spirited sense of joi de vivre will always see her right because greatness nearly always results from adversity.
Memphis: Ten times more useful than her male counterpart, Memphis has had no choice but to become reasonably loud and brash. She has a deep, genuine laugh and, man, you want to see her in a bad mood!
Meng: Jazz singer, beat boxer and naked gardener – you name it – Meng is a gorgeous brute of a woman.
Mercedes: Life’s tougher challenges.....is she up to it? Initially, one thinks not but then, the girl turns into a woman, and all of a sudden the swan emerges from the gloom as the graceful lines of her thinking propel her forward. Mercedes is a serious and regal cat, sure enough, but she’s down-pat with the things that matter.
Mercianne: Uncompromising. And ain't nothing wrong with a powerful woman. Imagine life in Syria, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Turkey, and Christ knows where else if most men understood and believed this quite simple axiom?...
Mercy: Mercy, can you please go and get a job! And if you're intend to keep living with your parents can you start turning the television off, or at least turning it down. And what's the deal with all these chip packets?
Meredith: A beautiful and caring woman who finds it difficult to believe people can be so cruel. Does it make her appear overly-concerned sometimes? Well, perhaps, but here’s the thing: whether or not she’s a mother, Meredith’s name wraps around you in a very complex and encompassing way. Ideally suited to dealing with unfortunate circumstances, Meredith would make a wonderful manager of a women’s refuge, a medical doctor or any kind of psychologist.
Merewyn: Merewyn richly deserves her prize, or the career, or the house, or the holiday, or the loving partner that she's always desired. It's not like she hasn't put in the effort, and she's no fool. Her parents are/were country folk who instilled her with a proper sense of right and wrong, not to mention a reasonably diligent work ethic. The older she gets the more playful she's becoming.
Meri: A cross between a mild case of Bali Belly (whose worst symptom is that it gives you something to think about) and a bed covered in the petals of red Spanish roses, Meri propels herself into the universe rather splendidly because she expects that great things will always happen.
Merilyn: The name of an old time waltz.
Merle:
Some situations just aren't fair, are they. I mean, on one level you've got it sussed: you knew the diff/axle problem was going to come to a head at some stage soon, and you've always had the equipment with you, because if nothing else you need to be prepared when you're living on the land, but why here and why now?

The winter you can deal with, and you can even deal with the fact that it's started to rain. What you find incredibly ironic, however, is that you've just discovered that the tarp you laid down under the truck has a hole in it, right beneath the nape of your neck where you're positioned (and no other body position will do). So, yep, the spanner is in your hand and you know what to do, but it's the cold, stinking cow shit seeping into your hair and collar-line through the hole in the tarp which is the real pits.

Son of a bitch, eh? We call this the Merle Factor, and for anyone watching it's funny, but they're not the one fixing the problem now, are they.
Merlyn: No, she's not a magician but she can foster a sense of purpose and well-being within a disgruntled group/family/council meeting/tribe gathering.
Merran: Peculiar and dancy, Merran dashes about as if we are all running out of time. Not that she’s ever unhappy. And she has lots of weird little gadgets in her bag. She's quite the mystery.
Merren:
Merren rarely wastes her time or energy, yet for a no-nonsense girl she does have a wonderful sense of fun. She's the sort of woman who, when confronted by a useless man who is trying to re-attach a new door into an old set of screw holes, or maybe a wimp on a game fishing trip who is suddenly too scared to lean over and gaff the giant tuna someone has just hauled along side the boat, will push the dud aside and take control of the situation. In both cases, some short, deft work by Merren will see the new door attached with precision, and everyone will be eating sushi on the foredeck tonight, G&T in hand. Indeed, Merren probably forgot to wash the tuna blood off her shirt. 
Bravo Merren.
Merridie: Merridie, Merridie, Merridie, Merridie, life is but a dream'.....until she wakes up and realizes she's missed a mortgage payment. But, she knows that in the long run, things like that don't actually amount to all that much.
Merrill: Another farmer. She has a keen interest in the weather and only those things that might effect the soil, machinery and the household. Having worked hard for most of her life, she is often viewed as being somewhat uncompromising but all she is doing is trying to instill those around her with the belief that hard work, persistence and an eye on the consequences of one's actions are vitally important to the success or failure of any enterprise. (She actually has a wonderful sense of humour.)
Merrily: Lopsided and lost, Merrily leaps from lily-pad to lily-pad, from person to person and from chaotic silly moment to chaotic silly moment like a smiling, bouncy little frog. She loves just about everyone and just about everyone loves her back. (She's failed to gain her driver's licence on no less than 27 attempts and I think most of us would secretly agree that this is a good thing.)
Merrin: Whatever you do, don't take her on a holiday to some boring resort with sun and sand, where everyone is walking around in bathers, smiling stupidly at each other and where everything is just a waiter's beck and call, away. Nope. This girl likes a task. You want to take her on a holiday, then take her to Canada in their winter and take her to the coast. Give her some overalls and a big filletting knife, and get her a job filleting Atlantic salmon all day. It's cold, it's wet and it's a physical challenge. But, the people she'll be working with are hard, salt-of-the-earth types who are funnier than any millionare comedian in Hollywood. Merrin.
Merryn:
No, Merryn doesn't work in a nursery and having had her kids, when she gets to grandmother status she wont be that keen to look after her grandchildren either, and rightly so. Like Neville way after her, she's not so delighted at what society has done to the modern world. But, Merryn seeks humour and love in the right places and she has quick wit.
As the lord says, ‘Blessed be thy Merryn’.
Mery: Mary’s unforgiving, complicated and loving cousin whose origins hail from the passionate Adriatic. Mery is delicious and intense, and worthy of only the finer men.
Meryl: Meryl works tirelessly for those around her and she has a wonderful sense of humour, despite laying down the law from time to time. It's a necessary part of the job. Anyway, she is entitled to as much adoration and holiday time as you can give her. But you know that already, don't you? You should.
Mia:
Option A:  Mia is a mound of fairy floss that you buy on a stick at the show. She is therefore very sweet and too much of her might make you ill.

Option B:  An Olympic Show Jumper that is full of guts, skill and grace. I kid you not.
Miah: Educated, sensual and not the first to act completely impulsively, Miah has particular requirements, be they for this moment, this life, tonight’s dinner or tomorrow’s meeting, and only once she’s satisfied does she feel like she has the space to be silly. She makes a splendid director of anything and she’s good at making love quietly.
Micaela: Dogmatic. Her decisions arrive devoid of emotional involvement and if there is a wrong to be righted she wont stop till justice is achieved, and how many times does she spell her name to people each week?
Micah: Precise in her movements; Punctual; Thoughtful. Micah has the most looked-after skin in the Kingdom which has the effect of making her resemble someone half her age. Little do most people know, however, that Micah can carry the world on her shoulders.
Michaela: Michaela is the name of any haircut that goes ‘Voomph’ across the forehead and ‘Voom-Voomph’ down the sides.
Michele: Diligent and lovely, Michele speaks beautifully, she is highly intelligent and she is a hopeless romantic.
Michelle: Yes, okay, so we once described Michelle as the name given to the sound of little waves washing up on a tiny coral atoll, having arrived there via a shipwreck or a plane crash. The moral to this story being that, Michelle, almost miraculously, can turn most potential tragedies into a sudden fluke of good luck. We’d suggest that this isn’t luck at all, but the result of a girl living well, and who is fiercely dedicated to making wonderful memories for herself, and for those she cares about the most. Not bad, eh?
Michka: The name of a type of dream where everything starts off great and then ends in utter catastrophe, possibly your own death.
Micky: Commercial diver. She gets paid a fortune but it's occasionally hard and dangerous work. But, she loves the money and deep down, she's tougher than most hard men.
Mietta: No, Mietta may not be a fully-fledged revolutionary, but she does seem to find herself repeatedly transforming situations for the better. If you're doing something underhanded, I wouldn't be telling Mietta about it. Yes, on the surface she's fun, and sexy, and she has a delicious smile, but if you're lying, or cheating, or defrauding someone and she finds out, you’re fucked.
Mignon: Intensely loyal and thoughtful, Mignon is a wonderful student.
Miho: True to form, Miho is the Japanese term for an incredibly long and wonderful sailing journey.  What a girl she is...
Mika: Sexy, contained and diligent with a gentle swish of self consciousness washed over it all, Mika is lovely.
Mikaela: Disorganised, well, yes, that’s probably true too, but as a younger lass does it really matter? She grows out of that, thankfully, and these days Mikaela is quick to act and decisive in her movements, which isn’t a bad turnaround really. She’s not afraid to approach men either, although her selection process might need a bit of work. Does she know what she wants, I wonder? If she can answer that in the affirmative then anything is possible!
Mikala: Mikala is obsessive-compulsive in at least one aspect of her life – possibly with regard to clothes and cleaning.
Mikayla: Decisive? Well, maybe not initially but she gets there eventually. Yes, she's distracted by her friends too much and yes, occasionally she might be easily led, but she'll grow out of that. She'd never walk in and take over a party, let alone get herself arrested, but she knows how to handle the books. She's actually quite organised.
Mikaylah:
Christ, how many times per week does she have to spell her name? Aaaanyway, Mikaylah is no fool, that's for certain, she has friends and she knows what she wants from romance, but at some point she’ll stop and look around her and realise she needs to get on a plane on her own, and just GO!
(Note to Mikaylah: Don't give in by taking a job which requires wearing a name tag - you're better than that!)
Mikenzy: Not the academic type, Mikenzy is more like the Hey-Look-I've-Just-Found-Ten-Bucks-Down-The-Back-Of-The-Couch-And-I'm-Off-To-Maccas-For-A-McCrap burger-And-A-Free-Pair-Of-Sunglasses, type.
Mila: Once upon a time we suggested you go and visit the male Reuben for Mila’s description. What were we thinking? Mila is like a beautiful wild mustang who refuses to be tamed…..at least, this is what we hope for.
Mileah: The coach is always yelling at her to try harder, to put more effort in and to think about what she really wants. She should just explain to the them that she is interested in natural therapies.  - this is what she's interested in. A tough, competitive environment isn't really her favourite place to be, you see. Yoga class - this is where she finds peace.
Miley:
“Ah, that’s bollocks!” she says.
The famous artist who has just finished her portrait has never received such a reaction, and he is aghast. 
“I mean, she’s got a cute face,” Miley continues, “but she looks nothing like me! Do you honestly expect me to pay for this?”

She knows the fate of western civilisation doesn’t hang in the balance here, and she’ll retain her sense of humour alright, but a deal is a deal, and everyone ought to do their best. And she’ll always make the call if someone isn’t. 
Miley.
Milla: Milla tends to keep it all shipshape. Yep, she knows everyone spells her name wrong, and she has to spell it out to people god-knows how many times each week but it’s water off a duck’s back. An optimist from the ground up, Milla presents front and square, and if she’s being a mischievous you’ll only ever find out much later, if at all. She’s a more capable leader than you imagine.
Milli: If Milli isn’t a cutesy-wootsie little puppy dog, then she is a gorgeous blonde human from the Czech Republic. In the case of the latter, whatever you do, don’t ask her if she’s from Czechoslovakia because that doesn’t exist anymore. I’m just warning you... (The Australian, English and American versions are much less dangerous, remembering of course that all Kiwis are sufficiently lethal.)
Millie: Mmm...a hell of a girl and hell of a blend, that being a mix of Alice, Daisy and Alex. Imogen too, if the planets line up right.
Milu: Milu is sensual and seductive, she detests liars, no matter what the circumstance, she loathes subterfuge and she's split up with boyfriends because they've bought her a meal from MacDonald's. If the oceans are going to be saved, and it might be too late, then souls like Milu will be the ones to do it.
Mim: A short name for a very long and out of control party which sees the cops being called.
Mimi: Not as cute and useless as she sounds. Mimi doesn’t take no for an answer and she certainly never dies wondering. Shocking temper, however.
Mimoza: Mimoza never travels light and she's held-up more planes than nearly anyone.
Min: A short name for an intricate personality, and one that folds over in on itself, like a new born baby cuddled-up in its cot in slumber. On the surface Min is gregarious, generous, worldly and incisive but all the while, deep down, she aches to be happy, and, primarily, to be loved. It seems that most people in the Kingdom wish for the same thing.
Mina:
As an auctioneer of some note, Mina can pick a movement or a thought from even the slightest change in appearance. And you have to be careful in her presence. A tiny nose itch or a humble throat scratch and you could find yourself needing to come up with 2.4 million quick-smart. My advice: do and say only if you really mean it!
(You may be interested to note that in a past life Mina was a bald eagle. She lived in Yosemite national park, in the good old U.S of A, and she could spot a hidden hare from 4000 feet.)
Minda: No, it's not Mandy, it's not Mindy and it's not Linda. It's Minda, okay? Hang on, where is she? She was supposed to be here an hour ago. Oh I see, she's gone to the wrong address again. Not to worry (sigh), we wont start till she gets here. Thank god she's not a priest. What's that? Her car broke down again just as she was pulling up? Oh well, we'll worry about that later. Minda, here, have a cup of tea and relax. It'll all be okay.
Mindy: Like a favourite CD that's started to skip but that you can't bare to throw out, Mindy attaches herself to your heart whether you are her friend or lover. Sure, she's slightly all over the place but what are you going to do? Not have her around? Anyway, after a while you realise that the CD skips exactly in time with the beat and, so, all she's really doing is giving you another avenue of appreciation. Mindy.
Minerva: It must have something to watch the Roman Colosseum in action. All those Christians tossed to the hungry lions in front of a cheering crowd. Can you imagine the spectacle? We would like to think humans have progressed but we're doubtful. If only we had more Minervas to deal with today's problems. Not a single evil bone in her body does she possess, traded off against complete compassion which is coupled with an overwhelming sense of experimental fun. She would have made a wonderful Jesus. She certainly wouldn't have stood around idly watching innocent people get slaughtered, either now or then. (And I'm suuuuuure all the religions of the world would just love a woman at the apex of their existence.) Anyway, if you happen to meet Minerva can you give her my phone number and tell her to ring me? Cheers. Management. x
Minnie:
Minnie approaches life like a big alsatian playing with a large, juicy bone, who doesn't want the fun to end. Which means she'll slobber and nibble and nudge and lick and toss around the said (metaphorical) bone, delaying for as long as possible the moment she decides to snap it into three places and get stuck into the marrow. After which point the fun-journey begins its end.

In life, therefore, Minnie's radar for fun times, potential patches of boredom and unmitigated buffoons is top notch. You might say she's busy, and you wouldn't be wrong. She'll call a spade a spade, and yep, if she accidentally ran over you on the farm with the ute, she'd get out that spade and bury you, say a wee prayer and tell the world that you must have taken off to go and see what's out there. And energetically-speaking she wouldn't be wrong. Minnie.
Minty: Like Deano way after her, you will never see Minty in times of depression or sadness. "Who's got time for that rubbish?" she'll tell you. And she's completely correct. Happiness is a choice for all of us, and the delightul Minty made hers long ago. In fact, bugger this, I'm going to her house. Who's coming?...
Mira: Where do you start? Her accent alone drives men crazy....
Mirabel: Mirabel, you can’t have everything exactly the way you want it all the time. I know you say you’re relaxed but, deep down, are you? Our advice? Go and kiss that beautiful stranger. What’s the worst that can happen? Most of all, BE RIDICULOUS sometimes. The End.
Mirabela: Way more raunchy than she imagines and completely adored by all who know her, Mirabela's success is no fluke. We're still surprised that it's a surprise to her, that's all.
Miranda: Neat, prissy and fussy. Miranda is nice until she’s angry although that can be said of most of us. She detests fishy smells and wearing the same clothes two days in a row.
Mireille: Mireille, I think it's about time you got your hands dirty. Try no-makeup for a week and see how good your face feels. Forget your nails, go and plant some tomato seeds in the back yard. After all, they're powered by the sun and the sun is free, but you will have to get outside away from magazines, not to mention all that pointless gossip of those dithering girlfriends. Maybe it's time to do something that scares the hell out of you?
Mirella: Mirella lets all the crap that doesn’t matter sail past her without so much as a second thought. She’s cool, she’s funny, she gets it, and she’s great at assisting others to see the moral of the story.
Miriam: Passionate for love and life, Miriam is an incredible optimist. Nothing gets her down. Nothing. In short, Miriam is a bloody legend.
Mishka: The out-of-control elephant who has escaped her handlers inside the main tent and is about to bring the entire circus to a stand-still.
Misspah: Misspah doesn't ever whisper. She can't anyway. She was brought up on some mountainous Pacific island, or maybe Papua New Guinea or somewhere, and so she's walks up and down great peaks all day, singing loudly. She has amazing hair, the largest lips you've ever seen and, yes, that means her smile is large enough to devour your heart.
Missy: Provocative on the surface and way more intelligent and interesting than she lets on…
Misty: Rarely macabre, Misty has energy and she is sufficiently sarcastic and in-your-face. Don't dilly dally if you're helping her with something, else you'll be given instructions on how to do it properly. She won't mean to be rude about it so don't take it personally. She's actually helping you. At least, this is the line of justification that she will take.
Mitch: Ever seen the movie Avatar? Well, you know the woman who flew the helicopter, and after a heroic set of deeds, eventually bought-it for the good of the team? I'm buggered if I know what they called her, but whatever it was they got it wrong. Her name should have been Mitch. She's sexy, she's funny, she's sarcastic as hell, she uses piss-ant men as a door mat and, by God, there simply aren't enough women like her. Amen.
Mlaine:
Wow, some parents are weird aren't they? Often they have no idea - just ask L_ah - but it seems on this occasion they fluked a diamond. Mlaine, you see, rhymes with 'Mmm-definitely', it rhymes with 'Mmm-not if he's a fuckwit' and it rhymes with 'Mmm-do you know what? I'm going to Italy, bugger it!'

She has time, she has a wicked, contemplative and mischievous smile and, best of all, no one knows what she's up to next. How is she successful then? I don't know, but she's definitley no fool. Anyway, if you can find her ask her for me. Good luck!
Mo:
Right, well, you better strap yourself into the seat of your roller coaster properly because there is an 11% chance of it coming off the rails, so try to enjoy the ride. 
(Note: Mo has a not-so-secret penchant for Big Trucks. She thinks they are, “Orgasmic!”)
Moana: The only time you’ll hear this girl moan is if she’s behind the microphone, singing the melancholy rifts to a rather splendid song. And she can move. And she’s beautiful. And she can paint. And….actually, how long have you got?……
Moira: The naughty little girl with freckles, who steals the odd toffee apple from the local milk bar.
Moko:
Moko is good at preparing for action. Have you got a good disaster plan? Do you have spare batteries? Have you got plenty of canned food? Is the bunker stocked with a supply of fresh drinking water? Have you got enough blankets? What about the first aid kit - is it up to date?
These are some of the questions she will ask you. When all of them are answered/solved then and only then will she smile and relax those shoulders. Moko.
Molly: Molly is that deliciously satisfying feeling you get after you rouse from bed in the morning, having made love all night long, and having had plenty of good sleep afterwards.
Mon: Whatever she's doing - and she generally does everything easily and with a simple grace - she needs to be married before she has kids. It's just how she is. And she's good with her hands, so try keep her out of any kind of office.
Monalisa: Monalisa can only come from one of the wierdest cities in the Kingdom - Las Vegas. She's black. She's beautiful. Indeed, if she's a white girl she's a whining waste of energy!
Monet: Really? Why not call her “Rembrandt”? Anyway, it’s not your fault your parents are twits Monet, but you’re polite and just a little unsure. Don’t be. You’ll soon see most of it is all just a grand irrelevant show, and that you can do anything you want. Why wait?
Monia: Monia acts promptly. Rarely given to displays of overt ostentation, Monia leads by example although she rarely observes her own behaviour that way. Most of what life presents is irrelevant guff and Monia understands this more than most. She therefore doesn't tolerate men/people who talk rubbish and aren't true to their word.
Monica: The inner tube of a tractor tyre that the kids inflate and take down to the lake to play with. And that’s all wonderful, but occasionally they return home with nasty scrapes from the valve that sticks out rather rudely. (For you dullards out there, what we are inferring is that Monica is vital to the team and the system, and truths need telling. Amen.)
Monika: Yes, Monika is a lovely girl but there are some doubts about her capacity to just relax and let the world slide on by if the time suits. She's be a nightmare on a three-day road trip, for example. Perhaps she suffers from a tiny bit of ADHD? We're not sure.
Monique: The living embodiment of a chook raffle. (What's a chook raffle? It's where a frozen chicken is raffled off at the country pub on Friday night at about 11pm. It's a loud, drunkard, crazy affair that makes no sense whatsoever, although they’re huge fun to both watch and be a part of.)
Monny:
Monny? Panic-stricken?……Often. Well, not really, truth be known. She just sounds like she’s panicking. Oddly enough in a genuinely dire scenario you’ll rarely see a more proactive and dedicated performer. Her laugh is loud, her orgasms are intense and she’s not far off being completely unembarrassable. Not so much a leader of industry as she is a leader of family and of a good time, in high school she got up to things at the back of class that we can’t talk about here. 
God bless you Monny. x
Montana: I wonder what’d happen if her parents had named her The Australian Capital Territory or perhaps Washington State? Anyway, Montana is an extra-double normal young girl whose sunnies are huge, whose jeans are low, and I have no idea what she’ll be doing when she’s 30. Does she exercise? Anyone?...
Moo:
Yep, Moo rhymes with boo, which is why she is the sort of girl who gets-off on concocting and videoing hilarious, diabolical and sometimes even painful pranks, and then sticking them on Youtube. On her gravestone needs to read the following: Never a dull fucking moment. 
Moo has a million followers, whether she's on Youtube or not.
Mora: Irish or not, behind the dusty curtain is a no-nonsense thunderbolt of sexiness, calm and humour who manages to get on with it!
Morag: Light-hearted and compassionate, Morag is in the Top 10 most dependable people in the Kingdom.
Morah: Irish or not, behind the dusty curtain is a no-nonsense thunderbolt of sexiness, calm and humour.
Morgan: Morgan believes she belongs on the edge of a polo field in her designer clothes, somewhere, doing whatever it is they do there. Is that the English form of cheerleading?
Morva:
What a fascinating creature. Before she exits her hole in the tree, she pokes her head up slowly, checking for predators. Soon, she makes her way out onto the limbs where others like her begin to mingle. Here they catch up on the latest gossip but soon it’s down to work, eating and feasting, and preparing the hole for another night. 
In human form she makes a splendid industrial engineer with a determined work ethic who, while a little bit shy, enjoys a well-mannered joke with everyone. Behind closed doors, however, is where her real inventiveness comes to the fore!
Moya: Moya will always find a way through. Do you know what I mean?
Muffie:
Muffie is out there, and she is one funny girl, besides. Take right now for instance. It's new year's day, and how do you think Muffie likes to bring in the new year? Yep, you guessed it – that’s her shouting out from up in that tree. That's right, she likes to herald in the first day of the year by climbing a tree with a bottle of champagne, a big fat doobie and as many friends as she can find who are game enough to go with her. 
Question: What the hell must she get up to in bed?
Mummacat: Mummacat is young at heart and she doesn’t take herself too seriously. As you might expect, however, she’d walk over hot coals and lift trucks for her children who are encouraged and loved to greatness and beyond.
Muriel: No one knows this so keep it to yourself.....in fact, come close so I can whisper it to you......did you know that Muriel is actually a superhero?.....and her real name is....Muriel the Underdog.
Murphy: Murphy is the leader of her pack. In the train carriage with her friends, and which they’re sharing with 100 other commuters, she speaks and laughs loudly in the hope that everyone on the train will hear her. Murphy.
Murran:
Revise revise and revise again: If you’re insistent about sending this letter of protest to the local council it needs to be water tight, especially if you’re going to put Murran’s name on it.
Don’t imagine however that she is some kind of Ice Queen. It’s just that she lacks time and she’s not used to having enough to throw at deeds of irreverent fun. 
Someone take her on a bloody holiday, will you?
Myf:
You know that scene in a western where the out-of-control train is flying down the track, all the controls are seized, the train driver has vanished and a lone heroine is in the driver's cabin with only a rifle? A fork in the track is imminent up ahead. If the train remains on the this track, though, it will hurtle off an unfinished bridge further along and kill everyone. But, there is hope. If the heroine can lean out and shoot the lever next to the fork with her Winchester, she’ll be able to change tracks ahead of the train and save everyone. She’s only got one bullet left. The moment is upon her. At 90 miles per hour, she leans out of the driver's cabin and takes careful aim, the wind blasting around her face...
“Yeah, well fuck this,” Myf says, nonplussed in front of the TV. “God, westerns give me the shits. Anyway, it’s my shout. Who wants a beer?”
Mykaela: Her name twists through your throat like a python around a hefty tree limb and I wonder if Mykaela is ever accused of being slightly unrepentant? The Buddhists talk about ‘letting go’ and giving in to your fears…at least I think it’s the Buddhists who promote these ideas, and in Mykaela’s case it isn’t bad advice. Then again, she’s a physical girl who is more competitive than she looks behind that cute and not-seen-enough smile of hers, so maybe we need to get her out on the field right when it looks like we’re getting beaten? What do you think, coach?…
Myla: Part Malaysian, part Indian and probably part English, Myla has gorgeous long black hair that she tosses over the back of any comfy chair that she happens to be reclining in. In this position she will listen attentively to anyone who is speaking unless she thinks they are full of shit, in which case she will sink further down into her seat and contemplate what kinds of fabric she might buy during her upcoming trip to Indonesia.
Mylie: Mylie needs minders. That is to say, somebody has to ensure her metaphorical bungee chord is properly attached. The boys in the commentary box have tried suggesting to her that, in all likelihood, her life isn't going to end at midnight, but they gave up long ago. (They pay her insurance policies for her, anyway.)
Myra: The Fruitbat. She looks kind of menacing and soulful, in a darkening-sunset kind of way, but she's actually very attentive and gentle.
Myrrhine: Some way between Miriam and Marilyn, Myrrhine is exotic and incisive, and not to be taken lightly. She’s the kind of girl who, if accidentally walking into the wrong theatre to watch a play that was never happening, and where a string quartet was playing instead, would take it upon herself to shmooze her way into one of the boxes where there was champagne, binoculars and an after-performance party.
